question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-2$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2) & =(-2)-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(-2)^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(-2)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯ \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡2 & =-2+\frac{8}{3!}-\frac{32}{5!}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(-2)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\operatorname{sin}⁡2.$
